The Committee <m Ritual:
Practically all of the Third Degree ritual is aimed at informing the Candidate that he is now as much a Master Mason as he ever shall be.
Portions of the Master's work of the Third Degree would have to be
changed to conform' to the intent of this resolution, as would the monitorial
"Master's congratulation to the newly raised Master Mason."
Under the conditions imposed by this resolution a Candidate would not
be permitted to sign the Lodge by-laws. What if the Candidate should ?ie
before giving the Third Degree proficiency? He could not then be buried
with Masonic honors.
Longevity toward receiving Veteran Awards would not commence until
the Candidate had given Third Degree proficiency, which in some cases
would run one or more years.
Many would not give Third Degree proficiency at all. This would cause
loss of membership to Lodges.
It is most desirable that the Candidate give Third Degree proficiency but
he can be educated in Masonic responsibility without so doing. This resolution presents far too many complications. We, therefore, urge a "No" vote.
The Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
Resolution No. 17 proposes that before a newly raised Mason may be
acknowledged as a Master Mason, he must pass a proficiency exami~ti~n in
the Third Degree in addition to the First and Second Degree exammations.
In 19391 it w~s proposed to Grand Lodge that after a candidate received
the degree 0£ Master Mason, he would be required to pass a ~tis~actory
Third Degree proficiency examination before being congratulated, signing the
Lodge's By-Laws, or becoming a member of the Lodge.
.
The Committee on Policy and General Purposes at that time recommended
a "no" vote, and a majority voted against the resolution. The basis of the
Committee's opinion was, primarily, that such an amendment would create
a new class of Mason, one in which the candidate had been obligated and
raised as a Master Mason and entrusted with all the secrets of that degree;
and yet, not being a m~ber of his Lodge, po~ibly for reasons ~ond his
control, the candidate's status would be unaffiliated and unrecognized.

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

335

The present proposed resolution goes even a step further, in withholding
i.citnowledgement as a Master Mason entirely until the proficiency is passed,
despite the fact that the candidate has been so obligated. It is also noted
that no proposal has been made to require the passing of a First or Second
Degree proficiency before recognizing a candidate as, respectively, an Entered
Apprentice Mason or a Fellowcraft Mason; although the logic involved would
appear to have similar merit.
I therefore move the adoption of this resolution, and your Committee on
Policy and General Purposes recommends a "No" vote.

SHORTEN FORFEITURE PERIOD
(20)
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:

WHEREAS, When a Candidate definitely expresses lack of interest in
placing himself in position to advance through the Second and Third Deg~ees,
either by ignoring contacts or communications, or through verbal or written
assertions to said effect, thus evidencing consent to forfeiture, or in any other
manner refuses to progress, actual current experience has demonstrated
futility of adhering to the five year period specified in Section 546, CMC,
before declaration of forfeiture of fees, and
WHEREAS, The continued listing of such disinterested candidate obviously prompts each succeeding Master to uselessly, and at times over
zealously solicit revival of interest (if such ever existed) damaging Masonic
dignity.
BE IT THEREFORE RESOLVED, That Section 546, CMC, First
paragraph after "will be declared forfeited" be supplemented as follows:
"Provided however that any time subsequent to his Initiation, a
Candidate, unless he is stationed abroad in U. S. Armed Forces or is
otherwise temporarily employed abroad, definitely indicates, by ignoring
written or verbal request from within the Lodge that he prepare himself
for advancement, or by verbal or written declarations makes it clear that
he has no intent to make such preparation, thereby evidencing consent
to forfeiture, the Master may direct Secretary at any time subsequent to
such indicated consent, to forward to such candidate a notice in the form
and manner hereinbefore specified".

The Committee on Policy and General P'IWposes:
Resolution No. 21 proposes revision of Section 546 California Masonic
Code which now provides that if a candidate does not present himself properly
qualified for the Second and Third Degrees within a period of five years
subsequent to his initiation all fees and contributions shall be declared forfeited. This resolution proposes reducing the five-year period to two years
except where extenuating circumstances are shown to exist or where a candidate verbally states his intention not to proceed.
It is the opinion of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes that
no particular good will redound either to the Fraternity or to such Lodges
as may presently be affected by the application of Section 546. It opens the
door, moreover, to question as to the validity of claimed extenuating circumstances or the evaluation of alleged verbal statements of no interest in
completing the Degrees. Shortening the period will carry no significant financial advantage to the Lodge and remedial physical or mental treatment
that might well be impossible in two years might result favorably in the
course of five years.
I move the adoption of this resolution. The Committee recommends a
"No" vote.

Service for Constituent Lodges, as adopted in 1946, and amended in 1957,
be now amended as follows:

to clarify all movements and Ritual.

(25)

WHEREAS Lodges may annually remit the accrued dues of those of its

remitted have an up-to-date dues receipt for only a few days m June of each
year; and
WHEREAS Probably very few Masons know that they can attend Lodge
and visit others' with a membership card that is up to a year in arrears; and

and show by hi; card that he is one who allows his dues to become in arrears;
and

the first paragraph of Sec. 577 be amended to read as follows:
"A Lodge may annually remit the accrued dues of those of its members

taken. Such action should be taken at the January Stated Meeting if

While your Committee on Policy and General Purposes concurs in the
concept that large funds should be placed under the control and safekeeping
of the Grand Lodge, for use of the respective Boards, we find that to achieve
this would require a new and more properly worded resolution than that
contained in the second resolve. Such a resolution can be best introduced
at the next Annual Communication.
I now move the adoption of Resolution No. 26 and your Committee on
Policy and General Purposes unanimously recommends a "No" vote.
The Committees on Jurisprudence and Finance have authorized me to
inform you that they concur in the recommendation of the Committee on
Policy and General Purposes.

of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes.

AMEND FUNERAL SERVICE
(27)
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, the fourth word of the thirteenth line on Page Seven of the
FUNERAL SERVICE as revised by Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California
October 1955, hereinafter referred to as the Manual, is SPIRIT, and
WHEREAS, the third word of the first line on Page Eight of the Manual
is SPIRIT. One is given to understand that the SPIRIT has winged its
flight to the unknown world; that the SPIRIT has returned to God who
gave it, and
WHEREAS, the fourth word of the third line on Page Eight of the
Manual is SOUL. One is given to understand that it is the SOUL which is
being commended to Almighty God, and
WHEREAS, the third word of the third line on Page Fifteen of the
Manual is SPIRIT. One is immediately aware that: (1) The liberated
SPIRIT is gone ..• it has flown away • . . it has "winged its flight to the
unknown world." (2) The SPIRIT is gone .•• it is not here ••. it has
"returned to God who gave it." And, (3) That at the casket it was the
SOUL which was commended; i.e. "Almighty Father, unto Thy hands we
commend the SOUL of our beloved brother."
BE IT THEREFOR E RESOLVED THAT: In order to conform to the
aforementioned wording and uniformity the third word of the third line
on Page Fifteen of the Manual be amended from SPIRIT to SOUL. And
that the amended wording be caused to read: " •.. commending bis SOUL to
Almighty God .•• ~,,
Respectfully submitted,
PATRICK A. WALTERS, M., No. 30

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

dation was created, and that this Annual Communication reaffirm such
supposed policy.
Also, there have been referred to the Committee on Policy and General
Purposes Grand Master Herbert A. Huebner's two recommendations concerning the California Masonic Foundation, namely:
"1. That the Foudation be requested to take appropriate steps to ratify
reimbursement to Grand Lodge for funds advanced during the fiscal year
ending June 30, 1971.
"2. That Grand Lodge make no further advance of funds for the use
or benefit of the Foundation unless the Foundation agrees to make reimbursement."
By virtue of enabling legislation adopted by Grand Lodge at the 1968
Annual Communication, the California Masonic Foundation was incorporated on March 5, 1969, as a tax exempt, non-profit corporation.
Its Articles of Incorporation provide that: "The specific and primary
purposes for which this corporation is formed are to receive gifts, bequests,
devises and contributions of every kind and nature, and to hold, use, administer and disburse the same . . . for the furtherance of all phases of
educational, charitable and scientific purposes."
·
Quoting from a "General statement of Policies of California Masonic
Foundation;" "It is a general policy of this corporation to foster and promote
within the limits of its powers, Americanism, a respect for law and order, a
respect for the Flag of the United States, for the Constitution and laws by
which we are governed, and through the medium of education, to teach young
people of all classes, races and creeds that freedom under law, as provided
by our form of government, is a priceless heritage."
By action of the Grand Lodge, the original assets of the Foundation
consisted primarily of the two Clubhouses at Berkeley and U .C.LA. The
Berkeley Clubhouse was sold by the Foundation for $266,000.00 on September 20, 1968. The U.CL.A. Clubhouse has not yet been sold. For upkeep
of the U.CLA. Clubhouse, $14,679.31 was spent in the year ended June 30,
1970, and $16,165.26 for the year ended June 30, 1971. In his Mes.5age to
this Communication of the Grand Lodge, Grand Master Huebner estimated
that today ". • • the Foundation holds assets valued in the general neighborhood of $1,000,000.00," represented by real property at U.CLA., the
funds derived from the sale of the Berkeley Clubhouse, and miscellaneous
gifts.
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes regrets exceedingly
the misimpression of the proponent of Resolution No. 29 in the assertion
that Grand Lodge once adopted as a policy the inclusion " .•• in the annual
budget of the Grand Lodge the sum of $50,000 previously used for the
maintenance of the Masonic Clubhouse for the . . . purpose of scholarship
funds in the control of the California Masonic Foundation."
As so carefully delineated by Grand Master Huebner on pages 34 and
35 of his Message, the proponent's error arises from a misunderstanding of

the events at the 1967 Annual Communication, when the Grand Lodge
received "The Report of Special Committee on Programs for Students"
containing a recommendation that ". • • annual appropriations formerly
devoted to the clubhouses be standardized at $50,000.00 and added to the
educational foundation each year as an appropriation from Grand Lodge."
As now pointed out by our Grand Master, at the 1967 Annual Communication "the Report was adopted, without reference to any specific provisions.
At that time •.• the Foundation had not been created, the Clubhouses had
not been sold, and no $50,000.00 appropriation was included in the budget
•.•" Nor was any such appropriation adopted at the 1968, 1969 or 1970
Annual Communications. And never has your Committee on Policy and
General Purposes at any Communication recommended that Grand Lodge
annually contribute $50,000.00 to the California Masonic Foundation.
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes also regrets that, of
the several special and general purposes of the California Masonic Foundation, thus far the Foundation has been able to work on only one - namely,
ltholarships - and on it ineffectively.
In the "Report of Board of Directors California Masonic Foundation"
to the 1970 Annual Communication, its President said, when requesting an
allocation of $15,000.00 from Grand Lodge for the year ended June 30, 1971:
"Interpolating at this point, may I state that we hope, eventually, to become
self-supporting."
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes concurs with the
judgment of Grand Master Huebner, set forth on page 34 of his Message,
that " •.• the Foundation should live within its own financial ability ...,"
even if this means drawing upon its own capital. It is our firm belief that
the impetus derived by the Foundation from the transfer to it of the two
clubhouses more than qualified it to be self-sustaining. We sincerely trust
that an early sale of the U.CL.A. Clubhouse will be effected and that the
Foundation will intensify its efforts to effectuate all of the purposes for
which it was created.
To put Resolution No. 29 before you, I now move its adoption.
The Committee on Policy and General Purposes recommends a "No"
vote on Resolution No. 29.
The Committee on Policy and General Purposes furthermore recommends adoption of Grand Master Huebner's two recommendations concerning the Foundation, i.e. that the Foundation be requested to ratify
reimbursement to Grand Lodge for funds advanced during the fiscal year
ending June 30, 1971, and that Grand Lodge make no further advance of
funds to the Foundation unless the Foundation agrees to make reimbursement.

The Directors of the California Masonic Foundati<>n did not report.
A majority voted against the resolution.

To the Most WMshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
The records of Grand Lodge, the Masonic Homes of California, the
California Masonic Memorial Temple and the California Masonic Foundation for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1971 have been audited by the firm of
Touche Ross & Co. Certified Public Accountants. Their audit reports have
been reviewed by this Committee. You will find these full reports in the
published reports and proceedings.
For the fiscal year ended last June 30, Grand Lodge expenditures were
substantially under the budget amounts adopted at last year's Communication, particularly in the area of Appropriations. Although this category is the
smallest item of Grand Lodge expenditures, averaging about 14 to 15% of
the total, it is the area in which is reflected the budget estimates of some
thirty-five Committee chairmen.
As is the case with any business operation involving the use of a budget,
the ultimate cost of certain programs may exceed the budgeted amounts and
there are necessary expenditures for which budgets were not originally provided. The resulting supplemental appropriations totaling $21,300 were approved by the Grand Master, as required by our law, and we recommend your
approval of his action.
Major increases in the cost of operation of Grand Lodge, comparing the
past two fiscal years, took place in the items of Salaries, Data Processing,
Insurance, Ritual and Inspectoral, Annual Communication expenses and the
publication of our magazine the "California Freemason".
The per capita revenue, together with Investment income, provided an
excess of cash receipts over disbursements of $41,000.
GRAND TREASURER'S REPORT

Much of the foregoing is set out in the Report of the Grand Treasurer.
His report has been reviewed by this Committee and found to be in accord
with the audit reports.
We extend our sincere appreciation to our Grand Treasurer for his continuing unselfish devotion and we recommend your approval of his report.
"CALIFORNIA FREEMASON" MAo:AzINE
The per capita tax of $.35 for editing, publishing, and distributing this
fine magazine has remained unchanged for the past four years. In our report
to you last year we expressed the hope that the expense involved would keep
pace with the continuing decline in yearly income. However, we encountered
a budget deficit of $7,782 this past year because, operating as we do on a cash
basis, part of this over-expenditure is applicable to the present fiscal period
as it represents paper inventory and supplies for issues in part of this period.
The cost of paper, supplies, postage and mailing services are constantly
increasing but our net membership continues to drop each year. This can
produce only one result, i.e. an inescapable increase in the per capita. We

Your Committee on Finance expresses its thanks to the Grand Master
and to the Board of Trustees for their action in assuming the cost of the
Endowment Board and the trip to Union Ciy, both of which will have a
favorable effect on the per capita tax.
CALIFORNIA MASONIC FOUNDATION

We have again provided $15,000 in the budget as a result of a request
from the Foundation arising from educational grant commitments coupled
with the fact that the U.CL.A. Clubhouse continues to remain unsold. We
have received from the Foundation Board of Trustees formal agreement providing for the refund of this $15,000 prior to June 30, 1972. An amount of
$15,000, therefore, has been included in the Income section of the budget
thereby avoiding any impact upon the per capita assessment.
The Foundation did not submit an operating budget to the Committee
on Finance for review.
Although economic conditions are currently pressing in all areas of life,
today my brethren, you are the benefactors of your own previous and generous contributions to this Grand Lodge.
The establishment of the Homes Endowment Fund, which you approved
and have continued to support most generously, coupled with the willingness
which rapidly eliminated the mortgage on this splendid Memorial Temple has
allowed us to enjoy a low and constant per capita tax. Had this not been
done we would be talking about a higher per capita tax today.
It is the considered opinion of your Committee on Finance that the
Budget for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1972, as prepared for your con·
sideration, is adequately and fairly presented to guide the conscientious and
dedicated members of our great Masonic Fraternity in prudent disbursements
of their funds.
We urge that every possible savings be inade by all concerned not only
in this period, but in years to come.
'
Such inatters in the Grand Master's Message and in the several resolutions and reports which have been approved by this Grand Lodge and now
require funds have been provided for in the following proposed budget.

Friday, October 15, 1971
At 9:30 A.M. Grand Lodge was called on, the Grand Master presiding.
This session was raised by Worshipful Jack W. Joe, Jr. Master of San Buenaventura Lodge No. 214. The invocation was delivered by the Grand Chaplain.
The minutes of the morning and afternoon sessions of Thursday, October 14,
were read and approved.

ANNUAL ELECTION
The Grand Master announced that the hour had arrived for the Annual
Election and directed the Grand Secretary to read the sections of the Constitution applying thereto.
The R. W. Lester S. McElwain, Verba Buena Lodge No. 403, was elected
Grand Master.
The R. W. William H. Price, Evergreen Lodge No. 259, was elected
Deputy Grand Master.
The R. W. Raymond A. Ebbage, Capital City Lodge No. 499, was elected
Senior Grand Warden.
The W. Burton Meyer, Jr., Golden State Lodge No. 358, was elected
Junior Grand Warden.
The M. W. Chester R. MacPhee, Past Grand Master, Golden West
Lodge No. 455, was reelected Grand Treasurer.
The M. W. Edward H. Siems, Past Grand Master, Plymouth Lodge No.
560, was reelected Grand Secretary.
The V. W. H. Douglas Lemons, Bixby Knolls Lodge No. 699, was reelected Grand Lecturer.
At the request of the Grand Master-elect, Most Worshipful Myron E.
Smith announced the names of the appointive officers as follows:
Grand Chaplain, Robert M. Young, Paul Revere Lodge No. 462.
Assistant Grand Lecturers: Burton 0. Young, Fruitvale Lodge No. 336;
Edward E. Seagle, Polaris Lodge No. 730, Ulysses G. Patropulos, King
Solomon's Seaport Lodge No. 260; Wallace H. Fiske, East Belt Lodge No.
391; George W. Perkins, Mizpah Lodge No. 378; Ernest M. Newton, Silver
Gate Lodge No. 296.
Grand Orator, Ralph W. Winters, Live Oak Lodge No. 61.
Assistant Grand Treasurer, Arthur Linsk., Loyalty Lodge No. 529.
Assistant Grand Secretary, Verne W. Hendrix, Mount Diablo Lodge
No. 448.
Grand Marshal, Arthur R. Kirk, Verba Buena Lodge No. 403.
Grand Standard Bearer, William Wong, The Gabilan Lodge No. 803.
Grand Sword Bearer, F. Jose deLarios, Francis Drake Lodge No. 376.
Grand Bible Bearer, James B. "Pat" Smith, Chico Lodge No. 111.

INSTALLATION OF OFFICERS
Most Worshipful Myron E. Smith, Past Grand Master, acted as Master
of Ceremonies and the officers, elected and appointed, were installed by the
retiring Grand Master in accordance with the Ritual.
The Grand Master's lapel pin was transferred from the retiring to the
incumbent Grand Master and the other chair officers exchanged the Arthur
S. Crites lapel pins.
Very Reverend Roland R. Bach presented the pin of the Grand Chaplain
to the new Grand Chaplain Very Reverend Robert M. Young.
Worshipful Burton Meyer presented the Grand Orator's pin to Ralph
Winters, the new Grand Orator.
The newly retired Grand Master invited Past Grand Master Laurence E.
Dayton to the East and presented to him a plaque from the Masonic Homes
Board and Grand Lodge as a token of appreciation for his wisdom, talent
and counsel in serving. He responded with remarks expressing his appreciation
for the plaque and for the opportunity to serve.
The retiring Grand Master was presented with a Past Master's Pin by
Past Grand Master, Edward H. Siems, Grand Secretary, and with a Past
Grand Master's certificate by Worshipful DeWald M. Baum, Trustee of the
California Masonic Memorial Temple. He was then presented with a Past
Master's apron by his son, Worshipful Harlan P. Huebner, Past Master of
Wilshire Lodge No. 445.

On behalf of the members of Grand Lodge, Most Worshipful Chester R.
MacPhee, Past Grand Master, presented a gift to the Junior Past Grand

liabilities, and fund balance of The Most Worshipful Grand Lodge
of Free and Accepted Masons of the State of California (a nonprofit unincorporated fraternal organization) as of June 30 1 1971,,
and the related statement of cash revenues and expenses for the
year then ended. Our examination was made in accordance with
generally accepted auditing standards, and accordingly included
such tests of the accounting records and such other auditing procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances.

above present fairly the assets, liabilities, and fund balance of
The Most Worshipful Grand Lodge of Free and Accepted Mason~ of the
State of California as of June 30, 1971, and the cash revenues and

BOTE C - Pension Plan
The Grand Lodge has established a pension plan covering
all full-time employees. Total pension expense for the year ended
June 30, 1971 was $9,300. Total pension expense for the year ended
June 30, 1970 was $11,700 including approximately $1,700 for the
Temple employees. All prior and current service costs have been
tunded.

NOTE G - Reserves tor Special. Purposes
The trustees have established various special. reserves to
which are added gifts and be~uests and other amounts which generally
are used at the direction of the trustees tor purposes other than
direct operating expenses. The assets represented by these reserves
are included 1n the assets of the General. Fund.
N~ H - Changes 1n Accounting tor Trust Fund

Effective JUly 1, 1970, the income earned by the George F.
and Laura E. Brigham Scholarship Fund was retained by the Fund. In
prior years, the earnings were transferred to the Student Aid Fund.
